source_text: IV. Εἷς δὲ ὀνόματι Κόϊντος, Φρὺξ προσφάτως ἐληλυθὼς ἀπὸ τῆς Φρυγίας, ἰδὼν τὰ θηρία ἐδειλίασεν. Οὗτος δὲ ἦν ὁ παραβιασάμενος ἑαυτόν τε καί τινας προσελθεῖν ἑκόντας. Τοῦτον ὁ ἀνθύπατος πολλὰ ἐκλιπαρήσας ἔπεισεν ὀμόσαι καὶ ἐπιθῦσαι. Διὰ τοῦτο οὖν, ἀδελφοί, οὐκ ἐπαινοῦμεν τοὺς προσιόντας ἑαυτοῖς, ἐπειδὴ οὐχ οὕτως διδάσκει τὸ εὐαγγέλιον.
thought_title: Quintus fears the beasts and volunteers are rejected
orientation: The writers of the letter turn from Germanicus to Quintus the Phrygian to explain why they do not praise those who offer themselves.
pass_a_gloss: But one by name Quintus, a Phrygian man having recently come from Phrygia, when he saw the wild beasts became cowardly. And this man was the one who forced himself and also some others to come forward as willing people. This man the proconsul, after begging him much, persuaded him to swear and to sacrifice. On account of this therefore, brothers, we do not praise those coming forward by themselves, because the gospel does not teach thus.

choices.why: Work brief glossary fixes this office as proconsul for the Roman governor presiding over the trial
Keeps literal change of state on seeing the beasts, matching the contrast with endurance
Keeps reflexive force to mark self offering condemned in the brief, distinct from being handed over
Keeps the two separate acts of denial named in the brief, swearing and sacrificing, without merging them

pass_b_english: One of them was Quintus, a Phrygian who had arrived recently from Phrygia. When he saw the beasts, he became cowardly. He was the man who had pressured himself and some others to come forward willingly. The proconsul pleaded with him at length and persuaded him to swear and to sacrifice. For this reason, brothers, we do not praise those who come forward on their own, for the gospel does not teach this.
